claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each constituent element.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy exhibits greater high-temperature plastic strain than commercially used pure tungsten.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy exhibits greater high-temperature toughness than commercially used pure tungsten.
High configurational entropy in WTaTiVZr stabilizes low-energy grain boundaries.
High configurational entropy in WTaTiVZr promotes chemically homogeneous grain boundaries.
Low-energy, chemically homogeneous grain boundaries are less prone to embrittlement.
The proposed grain-boundary stabilization inhibits crack initiation in WTaTiVZr under high-temperature loading.
The proposed grain-boundary stabilization reduces crack-propagation rates in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
The WTaTiVZr alloy initially has a random distribution of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
Matching the materials' grain sizes and other relevant microstructural factors isolates grain-boundary stabilization as the proposed cause of any performance difference.
At 1150–1200°C, grain-boundary-mediated processes are critical to the compared mechanical behavior.
Under mode-I loading at 1150–1200°C, WTaTiVZr will have a higher resistance to crack initiation than pure tungsten.
Under mode-I loading at 1150–1200°C, cracks will propagate more slowly in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
EBSD, TEM, and EDS will reveal more uniform and stabilized grain boundaries in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is applicable specifically at 1150–1200°C when grain size and phase distribution are held constant.
